stem: Which lesion is correctly matched with its level of left-to-right shunt?

options.text: VSD - left-to-right shunt at the atria
ASD - left-to-right shunt at the ventricles
VSD - left-to-right shunt at the ventricles
PDA - left-to-right shunt at the atrial septum
Venous hum - left-to-right shunt at the ventricles

explanation: VSD is the correct answer: it causes a left-to-right shunt at the ventricular level.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a VSD shunts at the ventricles, not the atria.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an ASD shunts at the atria, not the ventricles.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a ventricular septal defect produces a left-to-right shunt at the ventricular level.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a PDA causes shunting between the aorta and pulmonary artery, not across the atrial septum.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a venous hum is an innocent murmur, not a left-to-right intracardiac shunt.
